Q: Trouble getting R to read data values as numeric A:

The ... operator is unnecessary in this case. The code must be as follows:

candatamax <-subset(candata, candata$Mortality.rate>0.07)

Q: Trying to create a log file in sharepoint A:

I think you get the error on this line Set logWB = Workbooks("logs.xlsx") because Workbooks.Open returns a workbook obj and sharepoint paths can act differently sometimes and be unreliable, try this instead:

Set logWB = Workbooks.Open("https://[companySP]/logs.xlsx")

And you are chaining objects here logWB.logWS.cell... since logsWS already referenced the worksheet, use logWS.Cells(r, c)

On the Dim r As Integer instead of Integer, use Long Dim r As Long because Excel rows can exceed Integer limits.

I also noticed your URL is not right, instead of https://[companySP]/logs.xlsx you wrote https:/[companySP]/logs.xlsx notice the difference?

----this might also be okay might fix any upcoming issues---
Declare your objects at the top, so something like:

Dim logWB As Workbook
Dim logWS As Worksheet
Dim r As Long
Dim c As Long

and qualify your cells since inside an event a cell may refer to the wrong workbook

ActiveLogWS.Cells(r, 1)

Q: Power Automate: Update Outlook Event without "Spamming" Previous Attendees with Personalization A:

What you’re seeing is standard behavior for Outlook. When you modify an attendee list, it’s sending notifications for a meeting update. Unfortunately, the Update event (V4) action in Microsoft Power Automate does not expose a setting equivalent to the checkbox in the Outlook on the web UI: “Send updates only to added or removed attendees.”

Even when using Microsoft Graph and setting sendInvitations = addedAndDeleted, it only works if Graph can recognize that specific attendees have been added or removed. However, in a typical flow where you’re using a function like concat() to build a new requiredAttendees field and sending the entire list again, Graph actually recognizes that as replacing all attendees.

The best solution is to:

  1. Get current attendees from the event.

  2. Add new attendee to list.

  3. Send update.

The alternative is to use a SharePoint list for tracking registrations and send a confirmation email as a separate action from sending a calendar event update.
